# Overview

This in-class exercise follows Lesson 7. It models how easily the 3,125 hexagons covering Singapore can reach eldercare centres, using the **accessibility** and **catchment** packages.

# Getting Started

## Installing the catchment package from GitHub

**catchment** is not on CRAN, so it is installed from GitHub. This only needs to run once, so the chunk is not run when the page renders.

```{r}
#| eval: false
remotes::install_github('uva-bi-sdad/catchment')
```

## Loading the packages

```{r}
#| output: false
pacman::p_load(sf, tidyverse, tmap, accessibility, catchment)
```

# Importing the Data

## Importing geospatial data

The three geospatial layers are MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL, hexagons and ELDERCARE.

```{r}
#| output: false
mpsz <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial",
                layer = "MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL") %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3414)
```

```{r}
#| output: false
hexagons <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial",
                    layer = "hexagons") %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3414)
```

```{r}
#| output: false
eldercare <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial",
                     layer = "ELDERCARE") %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3414)
```

## Importing the OD matrix

```{r}
#| output: false
ODMatrix <- read_csv("data/aspatial/OD_Matrix.csv", skip = 0)
```

# Data Wrangling

## Supply

The code chunk below creates a new field called `capacity` and populates it with the value 100.

```{r}
eldercare <- eldercare %>%
  select(fid) %>%
  mutate(capacity = 100)
```

## Demand

The code chunk below creates a new field called `demand` and populates it with the value 100.

```{r}
hexagons <- hexagons %>%
  select(fid) %>%
  mutate(demand = 100) %>%
  rename(id = fid)
```

## Tidying the OD matrix

The code chunk below selects `origin_id`, `destination_id` and `total_cost` from the OD matrix, then renames them to `from_id`, `to_id` and `dist`.

```{r}
ODMatrix_tidied <- ODMatrix %>%
  select(origin_id, destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  rename(from_id = origin_id,
         to_id = destination_id,
         dist = total_cost)
```

# Computing the Distance to the Nearest Eldercare Centre

In the code chunk below, `cost_to_closest()` of **accessibility** computes the travel distance from each hexagon to the closest n opportunities, here n = 1.

```{r}
dist2closest <- cost_to_closest(
  travel_matrix = ODMatrix_tidied,
  land_use_data = hexagons,
  opportunity = "demand",
  travel_cost = "dist",
  n = 1,
  group_by = character(0),
  active = TRUE,
  fill_missing_ids = TRUE
)
```

## Joining the output

The code chunk below appends the closest distance to the hexagons.

```{r}
hex_acc <- hexagons %>%
  left_join(dist2closest) %>%
  rename(dist2closest = dist)
```

## Mapping the closest distance

`st_bbox()` sets the map frame, which all the maps below share.

```{r}
mapex <- st_bbox(hex_acc)
```

::: panel-tabset
## The Plot

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6.5
tm_shape(hex_acc, bbox = mapex) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "dist2closest",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                breaks = c(0, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, Inf),
                labels = c("under 1 km", "1 to 2 km", "2 to 5 km",
                           "5 to 10 km", "over 10 km"),
                values = "-brewer.blues"),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Distance to the\nclosest eldercare",
                                      position = tm_pos_out("right", "center")),
              col = "grey85", lwd = 0.2) +
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3, fill = "#D55E00", col = "black") +
  tm_title("Accessibility to the closest eldercare", size = 1.5, fontface = "bold") +
  tm_compass(type = "8star", size = 2, position = c("left", "top")) +
  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom"))
```

## The Code

```{r}
#| eval: false
tm_shape(hex_acc, bbox = mapex) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "dist2closest",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                breaks = c(0, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, Inf),
                labels = c("under 1 km", "1 to 2 km", "2 to 5 km",
                           "5 to 10 km", "over 10 km"),
                values = "-brewer.blues"),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Distance to the\nclosest eldercare",
                                      position = tm_pos_out("right", "center")),
              col = "grey85", lwd = 0.2) +
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3, fill = "#D55E00", col = "black") +
  tm_title("Accessibility to the closest eldercare", size = 1.5, fontface = "bold") +

  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom"))
```
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Learning diary
The median hexagon is `r round(median(hex_acc$dist2closest) / 1000, 1)` km by road from its closest centre, and only `r sum(hex_acc$dist2closest < 1000)` hexagons have one within 1 km. Here a short distance is good access, so the scale is reversed, dark for near and pale for far, as on the prof's map.

The code passes `hexagons` as `land_use_data`, so the opportunities it looks up are the hexagons' demand, not the centres. It still finds the closest centre, because every `to_id` in the OD matrix is a centre `fid`, the centre ids only go up to `r max(eldercare$fid)`, and every hexagon id up to that number has a demand of 100. I check this against the smallest distance in each row of the OD matrix.

```{r}
nearest_check <- ODMatrix_tidied %>%
  group_by(from_id) %>%
  summarise(min_dist = min(dist))

all.equal(hex_acc$dist2closest[match(nearest_check$from_id, hex_acc$id)],
          nearest_check$min_dist)
```
:::

## Converting the ODMatrix data frame into a matrix

In the code chunk below, `as.matrix()` is used to convert the ODMatrix data frame into a matrix object.

```{r}
distmat <- ODMatrix %>%
  select(origin_id, destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  spread(destination_id, total_cost)%>%
  select(c(-c('origin_id')))

distmat_km <- as.matrix(distmat/1000)
```

# Computing 2SFCA with the catchment Package

In the code chunk below, [`catchment_ratio()`](https://uva-bi-sdad.github.io/catchment/reference/catchment_ratio.html) is used to compute 2SFCA.

```{r}
df_2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  max_cost = 5) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("2SFCA" = ".")
```

## Mapping 2SFCA

The slide shows only the map, and the prof said the code comes from the hands-on exercise. `bind_cols()` attaches the 2SFCA values to the hexagons. I reuse the `acc_map()` function from my Hands-on Exercise 7.

```{r}
hexagon_2SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_2sfca)
```

::: panel-tabset
## The Plot

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6.5
fmt_num <- function(v) {
  sapply(v, function(z) {
    if (z == 0) "0"
    else if (abs(z) < 0.01 || abs(z) >= 1000) formatC(z, format = "e", digits = 1)
    else if (abs(z) >= 100) format(round(z))
    else formatC(signif(z, 2), format = "fg", digits = 2)
  }) %>% trimws()
}

acc_map <- function(data, var, title, legend_title, zero_label = NULL) {
  x <- data[[var]]
  if (is.null(zero_label)) {
    q <- quantile(x, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 11))
    breaks <- c(q[1:10], Inf)
    labels <- paste(fmt_num(q[1:10]), "to", fmt_num(q[2:11]))
    fills <- "brewer.blues"
  } else {
    q <- quantile(x[x > 0], probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 10))
    breaks <- c(0, q[1:9], Inf)
    labels <- c(zero_label, paste(fmt_num(q[1:9]), "to", fmt_num(q[2:10])))
    fills <- c("grey75", RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(9, "Blues"))
  }
  tm_shape(data, bbox = mapex) +
    tm_polygons(fill = var,
                fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(breaks = unname(breaks),
                                                labels = labels,
                                                values = fills),
                fill.legend = tm_legend(title = legend_title,
                                        position = tm_pos_out("right", "center")),
                col = "grey85", lwd = 0.2) +
  tm_shape(eldercare) +
    tm_dots(size = 0.3, fill = "#D55E00", col = "black") +
    tm_title(title, size = 1.5, fontface = "bold") +
    tm_compass(type = "8star", size = 2,
               position = c("left", "top")) +
    tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom"))
}

acc_map(hexagon_2SFCA, "2SFCA",
        "2SFCA Accessibility measures",
        "2SFCA",
        zero_label = "0, no centre within 5 km")
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Learning diary
`r format(sum(hexagon_2SFCA$"2SFCA" == 0), big.mark = ",")` of the `r format(nrow(hexagon_2SFCA), big.mark = ",")` hexagons have a 2SFCA of 0, because no eldercare centre is within 5 km of them by road. With plain quantile classes, the lowest classes all run from 0 to 0, which is why the legend on the prof's map repeats "0.000 - -0.001". So I give the zeros their own grey class and split the rest into nine classes, pale for low and dark for high, following the colour guides from ISSS608 Lesson 2.
:::

# Computing E2SFCA with the catchment Package

## Enhanced 2-Step Floating Catchment Area (E2SFCA)

E2SFCA gives nearer centres more weight. `step_weights` sets the weight for each distance band, from 0.01 for centres up to 5 km away to 1 for centres within 1 km.

```{r}
step_weights <- list(c(5, .01), c(4, .05), c(3, .1), c(2, .4), c(1, 1))
df_e2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  weight = step_weights) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("E2SFCA" = ".")
```

## Mapping E2SFCA

```{r}
hexagon_E2SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_e2sfca)
```

::: panel-tabset
## The Plot

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6.5
acc_map(hexagon_E2SFCA, "E2SFCA",
        "E2SFCA Accessibility measures",
        "E2SFCA",
        zero_label = "0, no centre within 5 km")
```

## The Code

```{r}
#| eval: false
acc_map(hexagon_E2SFCA, "E2SFCA",
        "E2SFCA Accessibility measures",
        "E2SFCA",
        zero_label = "0, no centre within 5 km")
```
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Learning diary
2SFCA counts every centre within 5 km fully, while E2SFCA cuts a centre 4 to 5 km away down to 1 percent of its weight. The two measures rank the hexagons with a Spearman correlation of `r sprintf("%.3f", cor(df_2sfca$"2SFCA", df_e2sfca$"E2SFCA", method = "spearman"))`, and E2SFCA has `r format(sum(hexagon_E2SFCA$"E2SFCA" == 0), big.mark = ",")` hexagons at 0. The steps act like a stepped version of the distance decay used in KD2SFCA in Hands-on Exercise 7.
:::

# Computing KD2SFCA with the catchment Package

## Kernel Density (Gaussian) 2-Step Floating Catchment Area

```{r}
df_kd2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  weight = "gaussian") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("KD2SFCA" = ".")
```

## Mapping KD2SFCA

```{r}
hexagon_KD2SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_kd2sfca)
```

::: panel-tabset
## The Plot

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6.5
acc_map(hexagon_KD2SFCA, "KD2SFCA",
        "KD2SFCA Accessibility measures",
        "KD2SFCA")
```

## The Code

```{r}
#| eval: false
acc_map(hexagon_KD2SFCA, "KD2SFCA",
        "KD2SFCA Accessibility measures",
        "KD2SFCA")
```
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Learning diary
`weight = "gaussian"` uses the weight exp(−d² / 8), because `catchment_weight()` sets the scale to 2 km unless told otherwise. There is no `max_cost` here, so no centre is ever cut off, and `r format(sum(hexagon_KD2SFCA$"KD2SFCA" == 0), big.mark = ",")` hexagons are exactly 0. That is why this map needs no grey class. A centre 2 km away still counts for about 61 percent, while one 6 km away counts for about 1 percent, so the far west only gets a tiny value.
:::

# Computing 3SFCA with the catchment Package

## 3-Step Floating Catchment Area

```{r}
df_3sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  step_weights,
  normalize_weight = TRUE) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("3SFCA" = ".")
```

## Mapping 3SFCA

```{r}
hexagon_3SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_3sfca)
```

::: panel-tabset
## The Plot

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6.5
acc_map(hexagon_3SFCA, "3SFCA",
        "3SFCA Accessibility measures",
        "3SFCA",
        zero_label = "0, no centre within 5 km")
```

## The Code

```{r}
#| eval: false
acc_map(hexagon_3SFCA, "3SFCA",
        "3SFCA Accessibility measures",
        "3SFCA",
        zero_label = "0, no centre within 5 km")
```
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Learning diary
3SFCA uses the same `step_weights` as E2SFCA, passed here as the fourth argument, which is `weight`. `normalize_weight = TRUE` adds the third step. The source of `catchment_ratio()` shows that each weight is multiplied by the hexagon's chance of choosing that centre, which is the weight divided by the sum of the hexagon's weights to all the centres it can reach. So a hexagon near many centres no longer counts its full demand at every one of them. This stops the 2SFCA family from over-counting demand where centres cluster. Because of the 5 km steps, `r format(sum(hexagon_3SFCA$"3SFCA" == 0), big.mark = ",")` hexagons are still at 0.
:::

# Computing M2SFCA with the catchment Package

## Modified 2-Step Floating Catchment Area

```{r}
df_m2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  step_weights,
  adjust_providers = function(w) w^2) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("M2SFCA" = ".")
```

## Mapping M2SFCA

```{r}
hexagon_M2SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_m2sfca)
```

::: panel-tabset
## The Plot

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6.5
acc_map(hexagon_M2SFCA, "M2SFCA",
        "M2SFCA Accessibility measures",
        "M2SFCA",
        zero_label = "0, no centre within 5 km")
```

## The Code

```{r}
#| eval: false
acc_map(hexagon_M2SFCA, "M2SFCA",
        "M2SFCA Accessibility measures",
        "M2SFCA",
        zero_label = "0, no centre within 5 km")
```
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Learning diary
`adjust_providers = function(w) w^2` is the modified 2SFCA of Delamater, 2013. The first step, where each centre's capacity is shared among the hexagons that can reach it, still uses the plain step weights. Only the second step, where each hexagon adds up the centres it can reach, uses the weights squared. A centre 4 to 5 km away then counts for 0.01² = 0.0001 instead of 0.01, so distance matters more than in E2SFCA. The package notes that once the weights are changed this way, the scores no longer add up to the total supply. The two measures still rank the hexagons with a Spearman correlation of `r sprintf("%.3f", cor(df_e2sfca$"E2SFCA", df_m2sfca$"M2SFCA", method = "spearman"))`.

The prof's plot chunk for this map draws `hex_3SFCA` again, while his code chunk draws `hex_M2SFCA`. I map the M2SFCA values.
:::
